# NeuralNg Popover

> Arbitrary, non-modal, trigger-anchored top-layer content from `@neural-ng/core/popover`.

## Generation rules

- Import `NeuralPopover`, `NeuralPopoverTrigger`, `NeuralPopoverClose`, and when needed `NeuralPopoverInitialFocus` only from `@neural-ng/core/popover`.
- Use a native interactive trigger with `[neuralPopoverTriggerFor]="panel"`.
- Prefer logical `bottom-start` or `bottom-end` positions; start/end follow RTL.
- Put any Angular content inside `<neural-popover #panel>`.
- Use `neuralPopoverClose` for an in-panel close action.
- Popover is non-modal and never traps focus. Use Dialog for modal workflows.
- Popover is not a command list. Use Menu when menu roles and arrow-key item navigation are required.
- Do not generate `appendTo="body"`; native top-layer rendering avoids clipping and stacking-context problems.
- Focus remains on the trigger by default. Set `popoverFocusOnOpen="first"` and apply `neuralPopoverInitialFocus` only when the workflow benefits from moving focus.
- Use `role="dialog"` or `role="region"` only when semantically correct, and provide `ariaLabel` or `ariaLabelledby`.
- Bind `[(open)]` for controlled state. Use `opened` and `closed` only when lifecycle details are needed.
- `closed.reason` is typed as `trigger`, `outside`, `escape`, `close-directive`, `api`, or `native`.
- Use `unstyled` and typed `root`, `content`, and `arrow` class slots for headless rendering.
- Do not create an NgModule.

## Canonical example

```html
<button
  type="button"
  [neuralPopoverTriggerFor]="account"
  popoverPosition="bottom-end"
>
  Account
</button>

<neural-popover #account role="dialog" ariaLabel="Account panel">
  <h2>Neural Admin</h2>
  <button type="button" neuralPopoverClose>Close</button>
</neural-popover>
```
